scenario_text: A fixed decoder-only language-model training stack uses P parallel input transformations whose outputs are aggregated before prediction. N is the non-embedding parameter count measured in billions, P is the number of parallel streams, and L is held-out language-model loss. This is a single concrete experimental setting, not a multi-group SLDBench reproduction. Literature anchor: the parallel scaling law of Chen et al. (2025). During evolution, retain loss scaling with N and diminishing returns in P; scientifically motivated refinements may concern aggregation overhead, routing efficiency, or saturation, not arbitrary polynomial features.
derivation_notes: Fixed single-setting seed based on the SLDBench parallel scaling-law family; log(P) gives diminishing returns from additional parallel streams.

scenario_text: A dense language model is trained with a fixed tokenizer-training procedure and corpus family. N is non-embedding parameter count in billions, V is tokenizer vocabulary size in thousands, D is effective training tokens in billions, and L is unigram-normalized validation loss. This is one concrete training configuration. Literature anchor: the vocabulary scaling law of Tao et al. (2024). During evolution, retain diminishing returns from scale and a meaningful vocabulary mechanism; refinements may involve tokenizer efficiency or vocabulary-capacity interaction, not arbitrary terms.
symbol_descriptions: effective training token count in billions
derivation_notes: Fixed single-setting seed based on the SLDBench vocabulary scaling-law family with separate model, vocabulary, and data power-law contributions.

scenario_text: A fixed pretrained language model is supervised-fine-tuned on a curated instruction-following corpus. D is the number of high-quality supervised examples in thousands and L is held-out fine-tuning loss. This is one concrete base-model and task setting. Literature anchor: the rectified supervised-fine-tuning scaling law of Lin et al. (2024). During evolution, retain the finite-data transition and asymptotic loss floor; refinements may describe data quality, distribution shift, or saturation mechanisms.
symbol_descriptions: number of supervised examples in thousands
derivation_notes: Fixed single-setting seed based on the rectified SFT scaling law; the offset B captures the small-data regime before the usual power-law behavior.

scenario_text: A sparse mixture-of-experts language model is trained with a fixed routing policy and a fixed number of active experts per token. N is non-embedding parameter count in billions, E is the total number of routed experts, and L is held-out language-model loss. This is one concrete sparse-architecture setting. Literature anchor: the MoE scaling law of Krajewski et al. (2024). During evolution, retain logarithmic scale variables and the model-size/expert-count interaction; refinements may concern routing saturation or expert granularity.
derivation_notes: Fixed single-setting log-linear MoE seed based on the SLDBench MoE family; effective-expert refinements are deferred to evolution rather than assumed at gen0.

scenario_text: A dense language model is trained under a fixed unique-data budget. N is non-embedding parameter count in billions, D is total token exposures in billions, U is unique available tokens in billions, and L is held-out language-model loss. Repeated exposure to the same finite corpus has diminishing value. This is one concrete data-limited training setting. Literature anchor: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models by Muennighoff et al. (2023). During evolution, retain finite unique-data saturation and diminishing gains from repeated tokens; refinements may concern data quality or repetition half-life.
derivation_notes: Compact single-setting data-constrained seed inspired by the effective-data mechanism in Muennighoff et al. (2023); U*(1-exp(-D/(tau*U))) is an interpretable saturating effective-token proxy, not a literal reproduction of every fitted term in that paper.

source_family: SLDBench lr&bsz; adapted from Li et al. (2025) Step Law
scenario_text: A fixed dense language-model training stack is evaluated across learning rates and batch sizes while model size and token budget vary. lr is learning rate, bsz is batch size in thousands of tokens, D is effective training tokens in billions, N is non-embedding parameter count in billions, and L is held-out language-model loss. This is one concrete optimization regime. SLDBench treats this as an open discovery task and uses a human-derived baseline adapted from Step Law. During evolution, retain a scale-dependent optimal learning rate and a finite-batch penalty; refinements may concern optimizer noise, schedule mismatch, or compute interaction.
expression: A/D**alpha + B/N**beta + C + K_lr*(lr - F*N**gamma*D**zeta)**2 + E_bsz*(log(bsz) + G*D**eta/bsz)
symbol_descriptions: batch size in thousands of tokens
effective training token count in billions
model-size exponent in optimal learning rate
data-size exponent in optimal learning rate
derivation_notes: Fixed single-setting hierarchical lr/batch-size seed based on SLDBench's selected human baseline; it combines power-law scale terms with a quadratic learning-rate basin and a finite-batch penalty.

scenario_text: A fixed language-model evaluation suite exhibits a double-descent-like relation between training compute and Brier score on a class of easy questions. logC is log10 training FLOPs measured relative to 1e21 FLOPs, and Brier is the held-out Brier score. This is one concrete evaluation setting. Literature anchor: the U-shaped/inverted-U scaling phenomenon of Wu and Lo (2024), used by SLDBench as an extrapolation stress test. During evolution, retain non-monotonic compute behavior and a finite turning point; refinements may concern asymmetric branches or a second transition, not monotone power-law substitutions.
symbol_descriptions: base-10 logarithm of normalized training FLOPs
Brier score at the turning point
log-compute location of the turning point
derivation_notes: Fixed single-setting U-shaped compute seed; the quadratic is the minimal stable non-monotone baseline before any asymmetric or multi-regime evolution.
